summary: US equities finished August 24 with a split picture that remained largely unchanged from the earlier report: the S&P 500 closed down 0.28%, the Dow added 0.26%, and the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.12% as technology shed 2.01% while defensive sectors including Consumer Staples up 1.67% and Financials up 1.23% absorbed rotational buying. The 10 year Treasury yield fell 0.72%, meaning bond prices rose modestly as investors sought safety alongside the tech selloff, while gold finished essentially flat at up 0.05% and Bitcoin gained 1.89% on the day. Overseas markets were calm with Japan up 0.52%, Korea up 0.74%, Australia up 0.68%, and Canada up 0.26%, while European bourses were fractionally mixed. The CNN Fear and Greed Index held at 55 Neutral, steady from a week ago and up from 41 a month ago, suggesting no panic and no euphoria. The single most important stock story remained the broad AI and memory chip selloff, with MongoDB down 6.5% and Micron down 5.8% on analyst caution around limited near term AI revenue impact. The week's key calendar events are still ahead: Wednesday brings preliminary GDP and Core PCE inflation, Thursday brings unemployment claims, and Friday features Fed Chair Warsh speaking alongside the preliminary benchmark payrolls revision.
